title: Example 17-9: Crossed-Out Letters in Sentences

illustrates.quote: When words are shown with crossed-out letters within sentences: a. Follow points in Formats, §17.11.1 a-c. b. Enclose the repeated word in an embedded transcriber's note to distinguish it from surrounding text. c. Explain this usage in a transcriber's note.

blocks.text: Words with crossed-out letters are uncontracted, then repeated with a hyphen substituted for each crossed-out letter. The repeated word is enclosed within transcriber’s note indicators.
`The heater` (he-ter) `in the room did not work.`
`Did you pack your gear` (ge-r) `for the camping trip?`

print.notes: Four sentences, each with one word carrying a single crossed-out letter, the hyphen-substituted repeat embedded inline (parenthesised here) rather than as a separate list.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.11.2', matches source). Modeled as a standalone TN (its own explanatory text, 17.11.2c, 'done') followed by four sentences; the repeated hyphen-substituted word is written here in ordinary parentheses (not enclosed by any inline-TN markup this flat print schema can express) because Emboss has NO inline/embedded transcriber's-note segment type (F-211) — this is the file's own expected mismatch: the given braille wraps the repeated word in `@.<...@.>` brackets inline within the sentence; Emboss can only emit that wrapper at block level.
